4800 Pension Fund Interest (income, no tax role)
ledger.payroll: One entry per payslip: Dr 1200 Bank (net pay), Dr 1410 APIT Deducted (the APIT), Dr 1500 EPF Balance (20% of earnings); Cr 4100 Employment Income (gross pay), Cr 4810 Employer Pension Contributions (the employer's 12%).
ledger.interest: When the annual statement arrives: Dr 1500 EPF Balance; Cr 4800 Pension Fund Interest.
ledger.withdrawal: Two entries, so the payout shows as exempt income without counting the fund twice: Dr 1200 Bank, Cr 4950 Provident Fund Payouts (tax role withdrawal); and Dr 5900 Provident Fund Balance Paid Out, Cr 1500 EPF Balance.

ledger.payroll: In the same payslip entry: Dr 1510 ETF Balance (3% of earnings); Cr 4810 Employer Pension Contributions.
ledger.withdrawal: Dr 1200 Bank, Cr 4960 ETF Payout (income, no tax role: a terminal benefit, not exempt); and Dr 5900 Provident Fund Balance Paid Out, Cr 1510 ETF Balance. At retirement it counts towards the terminal-benefit bands (0% on the first Rs 10,000,000); the rule sets don't compute terminal-benefit tax.

planning.note: Neither fund guarantees an income: both pay a lump sum. Model each as a balance growing by contributions and a crediting rate, paid out at retirement; the planning engine should treat them as provident (capital), not guaranteed income.

real_crediting_rate_assumption.basis: EPF's last declared rate (10.75%) less the 5% inflation target, rounded down; an assumption
